correctness.rationale: Arbitrary-field proof: biderivations descend because all bracket values lie in the maximal ideal; Jacobi is a triderivation and reduces to the three independent relations 2 q1+r2=0, q2+2 r4=0, q3+r5=0, leaving dimension 15 even in characteristic two. The identity-linear automorphism group has 18 quadratic coefficients; its affine translation image has dimension 6+2=8 since DxM+DyM=span{xz,yz,z²} and the residual action changes exactly two z² coefficients. A constructive gauge fixes P and those two coefficients, giving a unique seven-parameter section. Standard-library checker reconstructs Jacobi/gauge matrices from truncated monomial arithmetic; ranks 3,8 checked modulo 2,3,5,7,11; all 2^18 binary coefficient assignments enumerated yielding 2^15 solutions. The finite tests are corroboration, not general proof.

value.rationale: The problem is the natural space of second-order Poisson lifts of the Heisenberg linear Poisson structure on the 3-variable infinitesimal local algebra. The result is a complete classification of all labeled lifts and their framed equivalence classes over every field, not an arbitrary slice or an isolated numeric computation. The 15/8/7-dimensional cocycle/gauge/cohomology distinction provides a structural invariant and usable canonical representatives for further deformation and orbit study; the exact q^15 and q^7 counts follow without characteristic exclusions. No full Poisson-isomorphism or integrability theorem is asserted.
